title: Multi-Gigabyte Financial Audit CSV Export Out-of-Memory (OOM) Crash
businessContext: A compliance portal provides a button for financial auditors to export yearly transaction records (typically 3,000,000 rows, ~1.8GB CSV). Whenever an auditor triggers the export, the Node.js container memory spikes past the 2GB limit and Kubernetes kills the container with `ExitCode 137 (OOMKilled)`.
problemStatement: The export handler queries all 3 million rows from PostgreSQL with a single `db.query()` and pushes formatted CSV strings into an HTTP response stream using `res.write()` in a fast while loop without respecting stream backpressure or `readable.pause()`. The buffer memory fills up faster than the client can download, crashing the server.
constraints: Export must stream smoothly with flat, bounded memory consumption (under 80MB RSS).
Must respect Stream backpressure (`res.write() === false` and `drain` event).
Use Node.js `stream.pipeline` or database cursor stream.
candidateTasks: Explain how `res.write()` backpressure works and what the return value `false` indicates.
Refactor to use PostgreSQL Cursor stream (`pg-query-stream`) piped through a Transform stream.
Use `stream.pipeline()` to handle errors and clean up socket listeners on premature client disconnect.
hints: When `res.write()` returns `false`, stop writing and wait for the `drain` event on `res`.
Even better: `stream.pipeline(dbStream, transformCsvStream, res, (err) => ...)` handles backpressure and abort cleanup automatically.

testCases.name: Streams gigabyte dataset with constant bounded memory

alternativeApproaches: Generating the file asynchronously via background worker, uploading to S3, and providing a pre-signed download URL.
commonMistakes: Using `stream.pipe()` instead of `stream.pipeline()`: `.pipe()` does not properly forward errors or destroy source streams when the client disconnects.
Increasing Node heap memory `--max-old-space-size=8192` as a band-aid instead of fixing the streaming architecture.
